Time: 2 min. Teaching intent: Open the hour and connect it to the week's decision.
Talk track: Identify the physical asset, model, data link, and decision served by a digital twin.

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Set the evidence contract.
Talk track: A four-part twin map with a named physical specimen and update rule.
Expected answer / misconception: A named artifact with source and a check, not an unsupported opinion.
Visual: Input, reasoning, and evidence are separate.

R5: NIST, Digital Twins for Advanced Manufacturing | https://www.nist.gov/publications/digital-twins-advanced-manufacturing-standardized-approach

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Is a detailed 3D model automatically a twin?
Expected answer / misconception: No. Fidelity alone does not establish a data-connected, intended-use twin.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.
[Sources]
R5: NIST, Digital Twins for Advanced Manufacturing | https://www.nist.gov/publications/digital-twins-advanced-manufacturing-standardized-approach
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A model predicts a quantity for specified geometry, materials, loads, and boundary conditions; one run does not by itself create a twin. Trace the visual in order: inputs; model run; prediction. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: A finite-element warpage run at 25 °C is useful, but without a physical specimen, observed data, and an update rule it remains a simulation.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R5: NIST, Digital Twins for Advanced Manufacturing | https://www.nist.gov/publications/digital-twins-advanced-manufacturing-standardized-approach
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: A finite-element warpage run at 25 °C is useful, but without a physical specimen, observed data, and an update rule it remains a simulation. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. 
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.
[Sources]
R5: NIST, Digital Twins for Advanced Manufacturing | https://www.nist.gov/publications/digital-twins-advanced-manufacturing-standardized-approach

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: The twin must refer to a defined package, lot, tool, or process state, not an unspecified generic package. Trace the visual in order: asset ID; process stage; observed state. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: For a fan-out wafer case, record wafer size, die arrangement, material batch, and whether the observation is after debond or after grinding.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Pause for an individual answer, then reveal and discuss.
Talk track: Can a measurement from another process stage update this state directly?
Expected answer / misconception: Only after the stage difference is accounted for; otherwise the records are not comparable.
Visual: The diagram lists the conditions to inspect without marking the answer.
[Sources]

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A data connection must state what is measured, when it arrives, how it is checked, and which model parameter or state it changes. Trace the visual in order: measurement; quality check; state update. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: A measured warpage value arrives. Check units and temperature, then revise a specified boundary or state estimate; keep the prior model version.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: The intended use determines required accuracy, update frequency, and consequences of a wrong prediction. Trace the visual in order: decision; tolerance; consequence. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: A screen for gross wafer handling risk may tolerate different error than a final fine-pitch alignment decision; state the decision before choosing a model.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
